outcome: Presence of oxysterols in human breast milk
Concentration of oxysterols in human breast milk
In vitro antiviral activity against human rotavirus
In vitro antiviral activity against human rhinovirus
cohort: The study participants were twelve donor mothers providing breast milk at different stages of lactation (colostrum, transitional milk, and mature milk).
finding: The side-chain oxysterols 25OHC, 27OHC, and 24SOHC were present in human breast milk at all lactation stages, with 27OHC showing a peak concentration in colostrum that demonstrated in vitro antiviral activity against human rotavirus and rhinovirus.
cross-section timing: Colostrum, transitional milk, and mature milk stages of lactation
